texts.orig: Whilst martial law is the will of the éommanders; and is only limited by the customs of war and the discretion of those who adininister it, still, as far as practicable, the procedure of military law is followed, and military court is held on the same lines as court-martial. Charges are simply framed without technicalitics. The prisoner is present, the evidence of prosecution and prisoner is taken on oath, the proceedings recorded, and the sentence of the court must be confrmed according to the rules of the Army Act. Sentences of death and penal servitude must be referred to headquarters for con firmation. In the South African War (1899-1902) these limits of procedure were observed, and when possible will always be. are
